thread:
sec-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: plaintext credential fragment detected in partner logs (gcs://partner-logs-prod). Potential KMS ciphertext + metadata copied in logs. Please triage.
sara: Saw the alert. quick check looks like a wrapped KMS blob and an associated service account email. putting a triage thread here.
kyle: Can someone paste the exact log line? need to confirm if it contains raw key material or just ciphertext + metadata.
sara: copying snippet: `2025-11-02T12:05Z INFO backup: payload=CiABAA...==, kms_key=projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/ck-prod, sa=prod-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
jen: Ok so it's ciphertext referencing our kms key, not raw private. blast radius = that SA + any places that can decrypt with that key. still critical.
matt: Agreed. Primary mitigation: revoke that SA's short-term tokens, rotate the KMS key or rewrap ciphertext, and rotate any Vault secrets that may have been derived from this.
dino: We should also add a deny policy on that SA for decrypt until we validate. can we patch IAM quickly?
sara: I'll open a quick IAM change PR to remove kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt/decrypt for that SA in the prod keyring. tagging @kyle for review.
kyle: +1. make it timeboxed (30m) so we can revert if needed. also enable per-request audit logging for KMS decrypts in the project.
jen: Running an audit query now to enumerate decrypts in the last 48h: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND resource.labels.project_id="redwood-prod"' --format=json`
matt: Good. Also run a resource inventory to find where that SA is used: GKE secrets, TF state, Cloud Run, service accounts impersonation.
sara: I found two GKE nodes with workload identity binding to that SA and one Cloud Run job. listing owners.
dino: I'll put the SA into a temporary deny binding using org policy and create a Jira ticket for full removal.
jen: Vault note: any secrets that used that SA or that KMS key for wrapping should be rotated. vault-bot, can you generate a list of secrets with `transit` wrap using ck-prod?
vault-bot: Found 7 secrets in vault-transit namespace with key `ck-prod`. Paths: secret/ingest/config (3 versions), secret/backups/s3-creds, secret/importer/token, secret/legacy/archival.
matt: Ok action plan: 1) block SA + remove decrypt permissions (sara/dino) 2) run audit & inventory (jen/matt) 3) rotate/rewrap KMS key or create new key and rewrap ciphertext (security/infra) 4) rotate Vault secrets that depend on that key (vault team) 5) notify partner + legal if exfil confirmed.
sara: Who owns step 3? we should prefer rewrap vs immediate destroy to preserve decryptable data.
kyle: Infra team to create new cryptoKey version and rewrap blobs, then rotate key name in Vault. I can take point.
jen: On rotation sequence: create new key version v2, run `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=ck-prod`, then rewrap ciphertext: `gcloud kms cryptokeys rewrap --destination-key=ck-prod/v2 --ciphertext-file=...` test on a sample blob first.
dino: For Vault: will create new transit key alias and perform `vault write sys/rewrap` style operations (we'll use our internal rewrap script). need maintenance window for apps that hold long-lived cached ciphertext.
matt: Also push RBAC changes to prevent the SA from being re-granted by Terraform: add a policy lock and patch relevant TF modules.
sara: I've created PR #4287 that removes the SA binding from the keyring IAM and creates a timeboxed emergency role. link: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4287
jen: Audit results: I see 2 decrypt calls from that SA in the last 24h, both originating from a Cloud Run job `partner-ingest`. timestamps: 2025-11-02T10:12Z and 2025-11-02T11:03Z.
jen: That suggests partner-ingest used it to decrypt something. need to coordinate with partner access team.
dino: Contacting partner ops now. copying email template in #partners channel.
sara: Legal on standby. If confirmed exfil, we file incident with P1 and run full forensics.
matt: Short-term: rotate SA keys (delete keys, revoke tokens), disable Cloud Run job, and schedule re-deploy with rotated secrets. Who can rotate Vault paths?
vault-bot: vault-admins:jen, sara have write permission for `secret/ingest/*` and `vault/rotations` is enabled.
jen: I'm starting rotation on `secret/ingest/config` and `secret/importer/token`. Will bump versions and update deployments to pull new secrets.
kyle: I'll handle key rewrap and KMS policy lock. ETA 2 hours for rewrap + validation.
sara: I'll coordinate the deployment freeze and ensure Canary doesn't pick old ciphertext.
dino: Partner confirmed: partner-ingest was forwarding logs to a third-party backup bucket; they will delete the backup and rotate on their side.
matt: Good. post-rotation checklist: verify no decrypt activity for old key, verify Vault versions incremented, update TF modules, run regression tests for ingest pipeline.
jen: I'm updating the incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-455. adding timeline and current actions.
sara: Quick note: implement auditor alert rule to detect future plaintext-like matches with regex for `CiAB` prefix and kms_key patterns.
kyle: Added to monitoring playbook.
jen: Rotation status: `secret/ingest/config` rotated, Cloud Run updated to use new secret version, job re-enabled in staging, smoke tests green.
dino: IAM deny binding applied and PR merged to lock the SA.
matt: Good work. closing immediate containment. next: postmortem + policy follow-ups (RBAC hardening, TF guardrails, partner contract).
sara: I'll draft the postmortem and assign owners. thanks all :thumbsup:
jen: Leaving final verification window open 24h. will update if anything else pops up.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2025-455 transitioned to status "contained" at 2025-11-02T15:10Z.
